newsitem.title: USA: PSE&G to file $2.5 bln refinancing plan.
newsitem.headline: PSE&G to file $2.5 bln refinancing plan.

text.p: Public Service Electric and Gas said it will file on Tuesday a $2.5 billion refinancing plan to cover costs associated with a rate restructuring plan through securitization of generation assets.

PSE&G said it will pass along to its customers the entire amount of savings resulting from securitization but cautions if legislation allowing for securitization is not enacted, the proposal will be jeopardized.

In a statement, the company said it has accelerated its timetable on offering its customers a choice of suppliers and will offer 100 percent of its 1.9 million customers the option to switch their power supply company starting October 1, 1998. The new provider will come online January 1, 1999.
PSE&G said their timetable for offering a choice of suppliers to customers is 18 months ahead of schedule.
The plan would coincide with a rate reduction between five to 10 percent, the company said.

PSE&G also said they would impose a seven year cap on the major components of rates, which would absorb fuel risks for the next seven years as well as costs associated with operation and maintenance of its facilities.
The company said it will file its plan with the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities tomorrow.
